sections.title: Linear Differential Equations (LDE)
sections.content: Standard form: dy/dx + Py = Q, where P and Q are functions of x only (or constants). To solve, find the Integrating Factor (IF) = e^(∫P dx). The general solution is: y * (IF) = ∫[Q * (IF)] dx + C.

sections.title: LDE in Reverse (dx/dy)
sections.content: Sometimes an equation is linear in x rather than y: dx/dy + Px = Q, where P and Q are functions of y. Here, IF = e^(∫P dy), and the solution is x * (IF) = ∫[Q * (IF)] dy + C.

sections.title: Bernoulli's Equation
sections.content: Form: dy/dx + Py = Qy^n. It is reducible to an LDE. Divide by y^n to get y^(-n)(dy/dx) + P(y^(1-n)) = Q. Then substitute y^(1-n) = t. The equation becomes a standard LDE in terms of t and x.

sections.title: Exact Differential Equations
sections.content: An equation M dx + N dy = 0 is exact if ∂M/∂y = ∂N/∂x (partial derivatives). The solution is ∫M dx (treating y as constant) + ∫(terms of N free from x) dy = C.

sections.title: Equations Reducible to Homogeneous Form
sections.content: Form: dy/dx = (ax+by+c) / (Ax+By+C). If a/A ≠ b/B, shift the origin: substitute x = X + h, y = Y + k to eliminate c and C, making it homogeneous. If a/A = b/B, substitute ax+by = t to make it variable separable.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Forgetting to make the coefficient of dy/dx exactly 1 before finding P and Q in an LDE.
2) Adding '+ C' while calculating the Integrating Factor (IF). (It is not needed there, only in the final solution).
3) In Exact DEs, integrating all of N instead of ONLY the terms free from x.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 2 handles the most frequently tested JEE types: LDEs and their reducible form (Bernoulli), recognizing exact equations (Mdx+Ndy=0), and handling linear fractional equations.

tricks.title: Exact Differential for Product
tricks.explanation: Memorize standard exact differentials to solve complex equations instantly without formal integration.
tricks.example: x dy + y dx is exactly d(xy). If an equation is x dy + y dx = x dx, it becomes d(xy) = x dx → xy = x²/2 + C.

tricks.title: Exact Differentials for Quotients
tricks.explanation: Familiarize yourself with quotient derivatives. They appear constantly in JEE objective questions.
tricks.example: (x dy - y dx) / x² = d(y/x). Also, (x dy - y dx) / (x²+y²) = d(tan⁻¹(y/x)).

tricks.title: Bernoulli n=2 Shortcut
tricks.explanation: For dy/dx + Py = Qy², the substitution is always 1/y = t, which immediately leads to -dt/dx + Pt = Q.
tricks.example: Avoids the confusion of the y^(1-n) formula. Just divide by y² and substitute.

tricks.title: LDE Identifier Trick
tricks.explanation: If 'y' and 'dy/dx' appear only in the first degree, and they are not multiplied together, the equation is an LDE in y. If 'x' and 'dx/dy' appear only in the first degree, it's an LDE in x.
tricks.example: y ln y dx + (x - ln y)dy = 0 → dx/dy + x/(y ln y) = 1/y (LDE in x).

tricks.title: Quick IF for Homogeneous Non-Exact DE
tricks.explanation: If M dx + N dy = 0 is homogeneous but not exact, an integrating factor is ALWAYS 1 / (Mx + Ny), provided Mx + Ny ≠ 0.
tricks.example: Multiply the entire equation by this IF to make it an Exact DE.

tricks.title: Exactness Check in 2 Seconds
tricks.explanation: To quickly verify if M dx + N dy = 0 is exact, partially differentiate the 'dx' part with respect to y, and the 'dy' part with respect to x. If they match, proceed with the exact formula.
